memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He will bring on you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you. The Lord will also bring on you every kind of sickness and disaster not recorded in this Book of the Law, until you are destroyed. You who were as numerous as the stars in the sky will be left but few in number, because you did not obey the Lord your God." — Deut 28:60-62 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This passage carries a particular sorrow. God had once promised Abraham that his descendants would be "as numerous as the stars in the sky" (Gen 15:5) — a promise of overflowing blessing and life. Now that very language is turned around: a people once as countless as the stars would be reduced to a few. The blessing seemed to be unravelling because of persistent rebellion. It is one of the saddest reversals in the chapter.

And yet, notice a small but crucial word: they would be "left but few in number." Even in the depths of judgment, a remnant remains. God does not utterly wipe out His people. Throughout Scripture, this theme of the remnant runs like a thread of hope — no matter how dark things become, God always preserves a people for Himself.

This is enormously comforting. God's purposes are never finally defeated, even by His people's failures. The promise to Abraham did not ultimately fail, because God is faithful even when we are not (2 Tim 2:13). The remnant would return; the story would continue.

And that thread of the remnant runs all the way to Christ. From the preserved people came the promised Saviour, and through Him the true family of Abraham has become vast — a multitude no one can number (Rev 7:9). What sin diminished, God's grace in Christ has multiplied beyond counting. His faithfulness always outlasts our failure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God's purposes cannot be finally defeated?
2. How does the theme of the "remnant" give me hope in dark times?
3. How does God's faithfulness comfort me when my own faithfulness fails?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, thank You that even in judgment You preserve a people, and Your purposes never fail. When my faithfulness falters, thank You that You remain faithful. I trust Your unfailing plan. Amen.
